requirements.statement: The server-rendered sign-in page presents the supplied sign-in card and its observed controls and text.
acceptance_criteria: Given a visitor opens the sign-in page, when it renders, then a bordered card shows a 'Sign in' heading, labeled 'Email address' and 'Password' inputs, a 'name@example.com' email hint and a masked password example.

Given the rendered sign-in card, when the visitor views its controls, then 'Forgot password?' appears beneath the password field, a dark 'Sign in' button appears below it, and 'No account? Contact your administrator.' appears beneath the button.

requirements.statement: Activating the sign-in page's 'Forgot password?' link starts a password-reset request flow.
acceptance_criteria: Given the sign-in page, when a visitor activates 'Forgot password?', then the visitor can start a password-reset request.

requirements.statement: A password-reset request returns the same response whether the requested account exists or not.
acceptance_criteria: Given otherwise equivalent reset requests for an existing synthetic account and a nonexistent account, when each request is submitted, then their responses are identical and do not disclose account existence.

requirements.statement: Password-reset requests are limited to five per account per hour.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account has received five reset requests within an hour, when a sixth request for that account is attempted within that hour, then no additional reset request for that account is honored.
Given the same account has received fewer than five reset requests within an hour, when an eligible request is made, then the five-per-account-per-hour limit does not prevent that request.

requirements.statement: An issued, unused, unexpired reset link permits its synthetic account's password to be reset.
acceptance_criteria: Given an issued, unused reset link for a synthetic account before its expiry, when the holder completes a password reset using the link, then that account's password changes.
Given a reset link has already completed a successful reset, when someone attempts another reset with that same link, then it cannot complete another password change.

requirements.statement: An issued reset link expires 30 minutes after issuance.
acceptance_criteria: Given an issued reset link, when a reset is attempted at or after 30 minutes from its issue time, then the link cannot complete a password change.

requirements.statement: Successfully resetting an account's password signs that account out of every active session.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account has active sessions, when its password reset completes successfully, then none of the previously active sessions remains signed in.

requirements.statement: Every successful password reset notifies the account owner through the in-memory notification sink.
acceptance_criteria: Given a synthetic account's password reset completes successfully, when the result is inspected, then a notification for that account's owner is recorded in the in-memory notification sink for that successful reset.
Given multiple successful resets, when the sink is inspected, then each successful reset has an owner notification.

requirements.statement: The application uses Python 3.12 and Flask with server-rendered pages.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application implementation, when its runtime, framework and user-facing pages are inspected, then it targets Python 3.12, uses Flask and renders the pages on the server.

requirements.statement: The application uses synthetic accounts and an in-memory notification sink.
acceptance_criteria: Given the application is exercised, when account data and recorded owner notifications are inspected, then the accounts are synthetic and notifications are captured in an in-memory sink rather than sent through an external notification service.

requirements.statement: The application provides automated pytest tests for the evidenced password-reset and sign-in requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Given the project test suite, when pytest is run, then automated checks cover the sign-in presentation, reset initiation and response parity, the five-per-account-per-hour limit, successful reset, single-use and 30-minute expiry boundaries, session sign-out, and notification after each successful reset.

requirements.statement: The project documents the production limitations of the small synthetic-account, in-memory application.
acceptance_criteria: Given the project documentation, when it is reviewed, then it identifies production limitations of using synthetic accounts and in-memory state or notifications without asserting that this demonstration is production-ready.

requirements.statement: The project neither deploys the application nor adds deployment workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Given the project deliverables, when they are inspected, then no deployment has been performed and no deployment workflow has been added.
